reading.body:
Seventeen frameworks make up this collection with a combined 1,176,038 GitHub stars, led by TensorFlow at 198,351 and Transformers at 164,705, together accounting for nearly a third of the category's total stars.

The next tier, LangChain at 145,455, PyTorch at 102,709, and Unsloth at 75,440, spans a wide range of purposes, from general-purpose deep learning to agent orchestration to efficient fine-tuning, which shows this category groups tools by their role in the AI stack rather than by a shared technical approach. Licence choice splits three ways: 7 of the 17 frameworks use Apache-2.0, 6 use MIT, 3 use a custom licence, and 1 uses CC-BY-4.0, a more even split than the agent memory category elsewhere in this collection, where every tracked project shares one licence.

Microsoft's autogen, at 60,741 stars, also appears in this site's multi-agent systems category with the identical star count, meaning at least one project here is tracked as both a general framework and a multi-agent orchestration tool, which reflects how blurred the line has become between the two roles.
